rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus is highly infectious and commonly causes outbreaks in semi-enclosed settings such as hospitals, care homes, schools and cruise ships.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus commonly causes vomiting and diarrhoea and can spread through people, contaminated objects and surfaces.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Alcohol-based hand sanitiser does not reliably kill norovirus; soap and warm water are required for hand hygiene.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Bleach-based disinfection is recommended for contaminated surfaces because norovirus can persist for days or weeks.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: People with norovirus should remain away from work, school or nursery until 48 hours after symptoms stop.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: People recovering from norovirus should avoid preparing food for others until 48 hours after symptoms stop.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: UKHSA publishes national laboratory and outbreak surveillance for norovirus and rotavirus in England.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: UKHSA provides public guidance on symptoms, transmission, recovery and reducing norovirus spread.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: Norovirus risk depends on setting, contact intensity, hygiene, surface contamination, food handling, genotype, host vulnerability and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA norovirus prevention and outbreak control
rows.verified: UKHSA norovirus evidence is outbreak-, setting-, person-, surface-, surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA mpox guidance covers public advice, case and contact management, settings, vaccination and surveillance.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Mpox contact tracing uses risk assessment and categorisation to determine follow-up and public-health advice.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA provides separate information sheets for category 2 and category 3 contacts of confirmed mpox cases.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Eligible contacts of mpox cases can be offered vaccination to reduce infection or severe-disease risk.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: The MVA vaccine does not contain mpox virus and cannot cause or spread mpox.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Mpox vaccination clinics should conduct pre-attendance exposure and symptom risk assessment.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Symptomatic contacts should be directed for testing and assessment rather than routine vaccination-clinic processing.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA distinguishes clade I and clade II mpox and maintains separate technical and epidemiological resources.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: Mpox risk depends on viral clade, type and duration of contact, bodily-fluid exposure, setting, symptoms, immunity, vaccination and timing.

rows.source: UKHSA mpox case, contact and vaccination management
rows.verified: UKHSA mpox evidence is case-, contact-, clade-, setting-, vaccine- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
